It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

== History ==
It is located at the east end of {{ill|Kutsukake-shuku|Q3200704|qid=Q3200704}} on the {{ill|Nakasendō|Q1154479|qid=Q1154479}}, northeast of the {{ill|Yugawa River|ja|湯川 (北佐久郡)|qid=Q11563522|lt=Yukawa River}}. The founding date is unknown, but according to shrine tradition, around the {{ill|Tenchō|Q1373138|qid=Q1373138}} era, when Nagakura post station on the old {{ill|Tōsandō|Q1334011|qid=Q1334011}} was developed, it was enshrined on Mount Nagakura, and the former site was called “Moto-Hachiman.” Kutsukake-shuku stood about 400 m south of the current site until its relocation after a fire in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=An'ei}} 2 ({{ill|1773|Q7692|qid=Q7692}}), and Nagakura Shrine is presumed to have moved at the same time<ref name=A>Tanigawa (2000) p.224</ref>. The oldest stone structure in the precinct is a stone lantern from {{ill|Kyōhō|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}} 16 ({{ill|1731|Q6963|qid=Q6963}}), comparatively recent, supporting relocation with the post-town move<ref name=A/>. There is also a poetry monument to Kutsukake Tokijirō by {{ill|Shin Hasegawa|Q11653726|qid=Q11653726}}.

An alternative theory identifies Nagakura Suwa Shrine in Miyota, Miyota-machi (same district), where {{ill|Otai-shuku|Q3357559|qid=Q3357559}} was located, as the Shikinaisha “Nagakura Shrine”<ref>Nagano Prefecture Encyclopedia p.577</ref>.
